Program 240: Router/Dispatcher

import re

class Router:
    def __init__(self):
        self.routes = []
    
    def route(self, method, path):
        def decorator(func):
            pattern = re.sub(r'{(\w+)}', r'(?P<\1>[^/]+)', path)
            self.routes.append((method, re.compile(f"^{pattern}$"), func))
            return func
        return decorator
    
    def get(self, path): return self.route("GET", path)
    def post(self, path): return self.route("POST", path)
    def put(self, path): return self.route("PUT", path)
    def delete(self, path): return self.route("DELETE", path)
    
    def dispatch(self, method, path):
        for route_method, pattern, handler in self.routes:
            if route_method == method:
                match = pattern.match(path)
                if match:
                    return handler(**match.groupdict())
        return {"status": 404, "message": "Not Found"}

router = Router()

@router.get("/users")
def list_users():
    return {"users": ["Alice", "Bob"]}

@router.get("/users/{user_id}")
def get_user(user_id):
    return {"user_id": user_id, "name": f"User_{user_id}"}

@router.post("/users")
def create_user():
    return {"status": "created"}

Program 241: GraphQL Query Parser (Simplified)

import re

def parse_graphql(query):
    query = query.strip()
    
    # Extract operation type
    op_match = re.match(r'(query|mutation|subscription)\s*(\w+)?\s*{', query)
    operation = op_match.group(1) if op_match else "query"
    name = op_match.group(2) if op_match and op_match.group(2) else None
    
    # Extract fields
    def parse_fields(text):
        fields = []
        depth = 0
        current = ""
        for char in text:
            if char == '{':
                depth += 1
                current += char
            elif char == '}':
                depth -= 1
                if depth >= 0:
                    current += char
            elif char in ' \n\r\t' and depth == 0:
                if current.strip():
                    fields.append(current.strip())
                current = ""
            else:
                current += char
        if current.strip():
            fields.append(current.strip())
        return fields
    
    # Get body
    brace_start = query.index('{')
    body = query[brace_start+1:query.rindex('}')]
    
    return {
        "operation": operation,
        "name": name,
        "fields": parse_fields(body)
    }

query = """
query GetUser {
    user(id: 1) {
        name
        email
    }
    posts {
        title
    }
}
"""

result = parse_graphql(query)
print(f"Operation: {result['operation']}")
print(f"Name: {result['name']}")
print(f"Fields: {result['fields']}")

Program 242: OAuth2 Token Manager

import time
import secrets

class OAuth2TokenManager:
    def __init__(self):
        self.tokens = {}
        self.refresh_tokens = {}
    
    def generate_tokens(self, user_id, scopes=None):
        access_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        refresh_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)
        
        self.tokens[access_token] = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "scopes": scopes or ["read"],
            "issued_at": time.time(),
            "expires_at": time.time() + 3600,
            "token_type": "Bearer"
        }
        
        self.refresh_tokens[refresh_token] = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "access_token": access_token,
            "expires_at": time.time() + 86400 * 30
        }
        
        return {
            "access_token": access_token,
            "refresh_token": refresh_token,
            "token_type": "Bearer",
            "expires_in": 3600,
            "scope": " ".join(scopes or ["read"])
        }
    
    def validate(self, access_token):
        token_data = self.tokens.get(access_token)
        if not token_data:
            return {"valid": False, "error": "Invalid token"}
        if time.time() > token_data["expires_at"]:
            return {"valid": False, "error": "Token expired"}
        return {"valid": True, "user_id": token_data["user_id"], "scopes": token_data["scopes"]}
    
    def refresh(self, refresh_token):
        rt_data = self.refresh_tokens.get(refresh_token)
        if not rt_data or time.time() > rt_data["expires_at"]:
            return None
        old_access = rt_data["access_token"]
        self.tokens.pop(old_access, None)
        del self.refresh_tokens[refresh_token]
        return self.generate_tokens(rt_data["user_id"])

oauth = OAuth2TokenManager()
tokens = oauth.generate_tokens(user_id=42, scopes=["read", "write"])
print(f"Access: {tokens['access_token'][:20]}...")
print(f"Valid: {oauth.validate(tokens['access_token'])}")

import json

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

class ContentNegotiator:
    def __init__(self):
        self.serializers = {
            "application/json": self._to_json,
            "text/csv": self._to_csv,
            "application/xml": self._to_xml,
            "text/plain": self._to_text
        }
    
    def negotiate(self, accept_header, data):
        types = [t.strip().split(';')[0] for t in accept_header.split(',')]
        for content_type in types:
            if content_type in self.serializers:
                return content_type, self.serializers[content_type](data)
        return "application/json", self._to_json(data)
    
    def _to_json(self, data):
        return json.dumps(data, indent=2)
    
    def _to_csv(self, data):
        if isinstance(data, list) and data:
            output = io.StringIO()
            writer = csv.DictWriter(output, fieldnames=data[0].keys())
            writer.writeheader()
            writer.writerows(data)
            return output.getvalue()
        return str(data)
    
    def _to_xml(self, data):
        def dict_to_xml(d, root_tag="item"):
            root = ET.Element(root_tag)
            for key, val in d.items():
                child = ET.SubElement(root, key)
                child.text = str(val)
            return ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")
        
        if isinstance(data, list):
            items = "".join(dict_to_xml(d) for d in data)
            return f"<items>{items}</items>"
        return dict_to_xml(data)
    
    def _to_text(self, data):
        if isinstance(data, list):
            return "\n".join(str(d) for d in data)
        return str(data)

cn = ContentNegotiator()
data = [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}]

for accept in ["application/json", "text/csv", "application/xml"]:
    content_type, body = cn.negotiate(accept, data)
    print(f"\n--- {content_type} ---")
    print(body[:150])

Program 247: REST API Client

import json
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from urllib.error import HTTPError

class APIClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url, headers=None):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip('/')
        self.headers = headers or {}
    
    def _request(self, method, endpoint, data=None):
        url = f"{self.base_url}/{endpoint.lstrip('/')}"
        body = json.dumps(data).encode() if data else None
        headers = {**self.headers, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
        req = Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method=method)
        try:
            with urlopen(req) as resp:
                return json.loads(resp.read())
        except HTTPError as e:
            return {"error": e.code, "message": e.read().decode()}
    
    def get(self, endpoint):
        return self._request('GET', endpoint)
    
    def post(self, endpoint, data):
        return self._request('POST', endpoint, data)

from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect
from typing import List

app = FastAPI()

class ConnectionManager:
    def __init__(self):
        self.connections: List[WebSocket] = []
    
    async def connect(self, ws: WebSocket):
        await ws.accept()
        self.connections.append(ws)
    
    def disconnect(self, ws: WebSocket):
        self.connections.remove(ws)
    
    async def broadcast(self, message: str):
        for conn in self.connections:
            await conn.send_text(message)

    except WebSocketDisconnect:

Program 249: Rate Limiter

import time
from collections import defaultdict

class RateLimiter:
    def __init__(self, max_requests, window_seconds):
        self.max_requests = max_requests
        self.window = window_seconds
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)
    
    def is_allowed(self, client_id):
        now = time.time()
        # Remove old requests
        self.requests[client_id] = [
            t for t in self.requests[client_id] if now - t < self.window
        ]
        if len(self.requests[client_id]) >= self.max_requests:
            return False
        self.requests[client_id].append(now)
        return True

    print(f"Request {i+1}: {'✓ Allowed' if allowed else '✗ Rate limited'}")

Program 250: Retry with Exponential Backoff

import time
import random

def retry_with_backoff(func, max_retries=5, base_delay=1, max_delay=60):
    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        try:
            return func()
        except Exception as e:
            if attempt == max_retries - 1:
                raise
            delay = min(base_delay * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1), max_delay)
            print(f"Attempt {attempt+1} failed: {e}. Retrying in {delay:.1f}s...")
            time.sleep(delay)

Program 251: Caching Decorator with TTL

import time
from functools import wraps

def cache_with_ttl(ttl_seconds=60):
    def decorator(func):
        cache = {}
        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            key = (args, tuple(sorted(kwargs.items())))
            if key in cache:
                result, timestamp = cache[key]
                if time.time() - timestamp < ttl_seconds:
                    print("  [Cache HIT]")
                    return result
            result = func(*args, **kwargs)
            cache[key] = (result, time.time())
            print("  [Cache MISS]")
            return result
        wrapper.cache_clear = lambda: cache.clear()
        return wrapper
    return decorator

@cache_with_ttl(ttl_seconds=5)
def expensive_computation(n):
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return n ** 2

print(expensive_computation(5))  # Miss
print(expensive_computation(5))  # Hit

Program 253: Background Task Queue

import queue
import threading
import time

class TaskQueue:
    def __init__(self, num_workers=3):
        self.queue = queue.Queue()
        self.results = {}
        self.workers = []
        for _ in range(num_workers):
            t = threading.Thread(target=self._worker, daemon=True)
            t.start()
            self.workers.append(t)
    
    def _worker(self):
        while True:
            task_id, func, args = self.queue.get()
            try:
                self.results[task_id] = {"status": "done", "result": func(*args)}
            except Exception as e:
                self.results[task_id] = {"status": "error", "error": str(e)}
            self.queue.task_done()
    
    def submit(self, task_id, func, *args):
        self.queue.put((task_id, func, args))
    
    def get_result(self, task_id, timeout=10):
        start = time.time()
        while time.time() - start < timeout:
            if task_id in self.results:
                return self.results[task_id]
            time.sleep(0.01)
        return {"status": "timeout"}

tq = TaskQueue(2)
tq.submit("job1", lambda x: x**2, 5)

time.sleep(0.1)

Program 254: JSON Schema Validator

def validate_schema(data, schema):
    errors = []
    
    def _validate(obj, sch, path=""):
        if "type" in sch:
            type_map = {"string": str, "integer": int, "number": (int, float),
                        "boolean": bool, "array": list, "object": dict}
            expected = type_map.get(sch["type"])
            if expected and not isinstance(obj, expected):
                errors.append(f"{path}: expected {sch['type']}, got {type(obj).__name__}")
                return
        
        if sch.get("type") == "object" and "properties" in sch:
            for key, prop_schema in sch["properties"].items():
                if key in sch.get("required", []) and key not in obj:
                    errors.append(f"{path}.{key}: required field missing")
                elif key in obj:
                    _validate(obj[key], prop_schema, f"{path}.{key}")
        
        if sch.get("type") == "array" and "items" in sch:
            for i, item in enumerate(obj):
                _validate(item, sch["items"], f"{path}[{i}]")
    
    _validate(data, schema)
    return errors if errors else None

schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["name", "age"],
    "properties": {
        "name": {"type": "string"},
        "age": {"type": "integer"},
        "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
    }
}
print(validate_schema({"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "tags": ["ml"]}, schema))
print(validate_schema({"name": 123}, schema))

Program 255: Environment Configuration Manager

import os
from typing import Any

class Config:
    def __init__(self, prefix="APP"):
        self.prefix = prefix
        self._cache = {}
    
    def get(self, key, default=None, cast=str):
        env_key = f"{self.prefix}_{key}".upper()
        if env_key in self._cache:
            return self._cache[env_key]
        value = os.environ.get(env_key, default)
        if value is not None and cast != str:
            try:
                value = cast(value)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                value = default
        self._cache[env_key] = value
        return value
    
    def require(self, key, cast=str):
        value = self.get(key, cast=cast)
        if value is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Required config {self.prefix}_{key} not set")
        return value

Program 256: Middleware Pattern

import time

class MiddlewareChain:
    def __init__(self):
        self.middlewares = []
    
    def add(self, middleware):
        self.middlewares.append(middleware)
        return self
    
    def execute(self, request, handler):
        def build_chain(index):
            if index >= len(self.middlewares):
                return handler
            current = self.middlewares[index]
            next_handler = build_chain(index + 1)
            return lambda req: current(req, next_handler)
        return build_chain(0)(request)

def logging_middleware(request, next_handler):
    print(f"  [LOG] Processing: {request}")
    response = next_handler(request)
    print(f"  [LOG] Response: {response}")
    return response

def timing_middleware(request, next_handler):
    start = time.time()
    response = next_handler(request)
    print(f"  [TIME] {time.time() - start:.4f}s")
    return response

def auth_middleware(request, next_handler):
    if request.get("auth"):
        return next_handler(request)
    return {"error": "Unauthorized"}

chain = MiddlewareChain()
chain.add(logging_middleware).add(timing_middleware).add(auth_middleware)

handler = lambda req: {"status": "ok", "data": req.get("data")}
result = chain.execute({"auth": True, "data": "hello"}, handler)
print(f"Final: {result}")

Program 258: URL Router

import re

class Router:
    def __init__(self):
        self.routes = []
    
    def route(self, pattern, method="GET"):
        def decorator(func):
            regex = re.sub(r'{(\w+)}', r'(?P<\1>[^/]+)', pattern)
            self.routes.append((method, re.compile(f'^{regex}$'), func))
            return func
        return decorator
    
    def match(self, method, path):
        for route_method, regex, handler in self.routes:
            if route_method == method:
                match = regex.match(path)
                if match:
                    return handler, match.groupdict()
        return None, {}

router = Router()

def get_user(user_id):
    return {"user_id": user_id}

@router.route("/users/{user_id}/posts/{post_id}")
def get_post(user_id, post_id):

import json
from datetime import datetime

class RequestLogger:
    def __init__(self):
        self.logs = []
    
    def log_request(self, method, path, body=None, headers=None):
        entry = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "method": method,
            "path": path,
            "body_size": len(json.dumps(body)) if body else 0,
            "headers": dict(headers) if headers else {}

        entry = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),

            "body_size": len(json.dumps(body)) if body else 0,
            "duration_ms": duration_ms
        }
        self.logs.append(entry)
        return entry
    
    def get_stats(self):
        return {
            "total_logs": len(self.logs),
            "status_codes": {l.get("status"): sum(1 for x in self.logs if x.get("status") == l.get("status"))
                           for l in self.logs if "status" in l}
        }

Program 261: API Pagination

def paginate(items, page=1, per_page=10):
    total = len(items)
    total_pages = (total + per_page - 1) // per_page
    start = (page - 1) * per_page
    end = start + per_page
    
    return {
        "data": items[start:end],
        "pagination": {
            "page": page,
            "per_page": per_page,
            "total": total,
            "total_pages": total_pages,
            "has_next": page < total_pages,
            "has_prev": page > 1,
        }
    }

Program 262: File Watcher

import os
import time
import hashlib

class FileWatcher:
    def __init__(self, paths):
        self.paths = paths
        self.hashes = {}
        self._update_hashes()
    
    def _file_hash(self, path):
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            return None
        with open(path, 'rb') as f:
            return hashlib.md5(f.read()).hexdigest()
    
    def _update_hashes(self):
        for path in self.paths:
            self.hashes[path] = self._file_hash(path)
    
    def check_changes(self):
        changes = []
        for path in self.paths:
            new_hash = self._file_hash(path)
            if new_hash != self.hashes.get(path):
                change_type = "modified" if self.hashes.get(path) else "created"
                if new_hash is None:
                    change_type = "deleted"
                changes.append({"path": path, "type": change_type})
                self.hashes[path] = new_hash
        return changes

Program 263: CLI Argument Parser

import sys

class CLIParser:
    def __init__(self, description=""):
        self.description = description
        self.args = {}
        self.flags = {}
    
    def add_argument(self, name, type=str, default=None, required=False, help=""):
        self.args[name] = {"type": type, "default": default, "required": required, "help": help}
    
    def add_flag(self, name, help=""):
        self.flags[name] = {"help": help}
    
    def parse(self, argv=None):
        argv = argv or sys.argv[1:]
        result = {k: v["default"] for k, v in self.args.items()}
        
        i = 0
        while i < len(argv):
            key = argv[i].lstrip('-')
            if key in self.flags:
                result[key] = True
                i += 1
            elif key in self.args and i + 1 < len(argv):
                result[key] = self.args[key]["type"](argv[i + 1])
                i += 2
            else:
                i += 1
        
        for name, spec in self.args.items():
            if spec["required"] and result.get(name) is None:
                raise ValueError(f"--{name} is required")
        return result

parser = CLIParser("ML Training")
parser.add_argument("epochs", type=int, default=10)
parser.add_argument("lr", type=float, default=0.001)
parser.add_flag("verbose")

Program 264: YAML-like Config Parser

def parse_simple_yaml(text):
    result = {}
    stack = [(result, -1)]
    
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
            continue
        
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        
        while stack and stack[-1][1] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        
        if ':' in stripped:
            key, _, value = stripped.partition(':')
            key = key.strip()
            value = value.strip()
            
            parent = stack[-1][0]
            
            if value:
                # Try numeric conversion
                try:
                    value = int(value)
                except ValueError:
                    try:
                        value = float(value)
                    except ValueError:
                        if value.lower() in ('true', 'false'):
                            value = value.lower() == 'true'
            else:
                value = {}
                stack.append((value, indent))
            
            parent[key] = value
    
    return result

config = """
# ML Config
model:
  name: resnet50
  epochs: 100
  learning_rate: 0.001
training:
  batch_size: 32
  use_gpu: true
"""
parsed = parse_simple_yaml(config)
print(parsed)

import queue
import threading
import time

class ConnectionPool:
    def __init__(self, max_connections=5):
        self.pool = queue.Queue(maxsize=max_connections)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        for i in range(max_connections):
            self.pool.put({"id": i, "created": time.time()})
    
    def get_connection(self, timeout=5):
        try:
            return self.pool.get(timeout=timeout)
        except queue.Empty:
            raise RuntimeError("No connections available")
    
    def release_connection(self, conn):
        self.pool.put(conn)
    
    def __enter__(self):
        self._conn = self.get_connection()
        return self._conn
    
    def __exit__(self, *args):
        self.release_connection(self._conn)

Program 266: Event Emitter Pattern

from collections import defaultdict

class EventEmitter:
    def __init__(self):
        self._listeners = defaultdict(list)
    
    def on(self, event, callback):
        self._listeners[event].append(callback)
        return self
    
    def off(self, event, callback=None):
        if callback:
            self._listeners[event].remove(callback)
        else:
            del self._listeners[event]
    
    def emit(self, event, *args, **kwargs):
        for callback in self._listeners[event]:
            callback(*args, **kwargs)

Program 267: Circuit Breaker Pattern

import time

class CircuitBreaker:
    CLOSED = "closed"
    OPEN = "open"
    HALF_OPEN = "half_open"
    
    def __init__(self, failure_threshold=3, recovery_timeout=5):
        self.failure_threshold = failure_threshold
        self.recovery_timeout = recovery_timeout
        self.failures = 0
        self.state = self.CLOSED
        self.last_failure_time = None
    
    def call(self, func, *args):
        if self.state == self.OPEN:
            if time.time() - self.last_failure_time > self.recovery_timeout:
                self.state = self.HALF_OPEN
            else:
                raise RuntimeError("Circuit is OPEN")
        
        try:
            result = func(*args)
            if self.state == self.HALF_OPEN:
                self.state = self.CLOSED
                self.failures = 0
            return result
        except Exception as e:
            self.failures += 1
            self.last_failure_time = time.time()
            if self.failures >= self.failure_threshold:
                self.state = self.OPEN
            raise

cb = CircuitBreaker(failure_threshold=2, recovery_timeout=1)
for i in range(4):
    try:
        cb.call(lambda: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ConnectionError("fail")))
    except (ConnectionError, RuntimeError) as e:
        print(f"Call {i+1}: {e} (state: {cb.state})")

Program 268: JSON Web Token (JWT) — Simplified

import hashlib
import json
import base64
import time

def base64url_encode(data):
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps(data).encode()).decode().rstrip('=')

def create_jwt(payload, secret, expiry_seconds=3600):
    header = {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}
    payload["exp"] = int(time.time()) + expiry_seconds
    
    header_b64 = base64url_encode(header)
    payload_b64 = base64url_encode(payload)
    
    signature = hashlib.sha256(f"{header_b64}.{payload_b64}.{secret}".encode()).hexdigest()
    return f"{header_b64}.{payload_b64}.{signature}"

def verify_jwt(token, secret):
    parts = token.split('.')
    if len(parts) != 3:
        return None
    expected_sig = hashlib.sha256(f"{parts[0]}.{parts[1]}.{secret}".encode()).hexdigest()
    if parts[2] != expected_sig:
        return None
    payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(parts[1] + '=='))
    if payload.get("exp", 0) < time.time():
        return None
    return payload

token = create_jwt({"user": "alice", "role": "admin"}, "secret123")
print(f"Token: {token[:50]}...")
payload = verify_jwt(token, "secret123")
print(f"Verified: {payload}")

Program 269: Logging Framework

import time
from enum import IntEnum

class LogLevel(IntEnum):
    DEBUG = 10
    INFO = 20
    WARNING = 30
    ERROR = 40
    CRITICAL = 50

class Logger:
    def __init__(self, name, level=LogLevel.INFO):
        self.name = name
        self.level = level
        self.handlers = []
    
    def add_handler(self, handler):
        self.handlers.append(handler)
    
    def _log(self, level, message):
        if level >= self.level:
            record = {
                "time": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                "level": level.name,
                "logger": self.name,
                "message": message
            }
            for handler in self.handlers:
                handler(record)
    
    def debug(self, msg): self._log(LogLevel.DEBUG, msg)
    def info(self, msg): self._log(LogLevel.INFO, msg)
    def warning(self, msg): self._log(LogLevel.WARNING, msg)
    def error(self, msg): self._log(LogLevel.ERROR, msg)

console_handler = lambda r: print(f"[{r['time']}] {r['level']:>8} | {r['logger']} | {r['message']}")
logger = Logger("ml_pipeline", LogLevel.INFO)
logger.add_handler(console_handler)
logger.info("Training started")
logger.warning("GPU memory low")
logger.debug("This won't show")

Program 270: Data Validation Pipeline

from typing import List, Callable, Any

class Validator:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rules: List[tuple] = []
    
    def add_rule(self, field, check: Callable, message: str):
        self.rules.append((field, check, message))
        return self
    
    def validate(self, data: dict) -> dict:
        errors = {}
        for field, check, message in self.rules:
            value = data.get(field)
            if not check(value):
                errors.setdefault(field, []).append(message)
        return errors if errors else None

Program 271: Pub/Sub Message Broker

from collections import defaultdict
import threading

class MessageBroker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.topics = defaultdict(list)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    
    def subscribe(self, topic, callback):
        with self.lock:
            self.topics[topic].append(callback)
    
    def publish(self, topic, message):
        with self.lock:
            subscribers = list(self.topics[topic])
        for callback in subscribers:
            callback(topic, message)
    
    def unsubscribe(self, topic, callback):
        with self.lock:
            self.topics[topic].remove(callback)

broker = MessageBroker()
broker.subscribe("model.trained", lambda t, m: print(f"  [{t}] Saving: {m}"))
broker.subscribe("model.trained", lambda t, m: print(f"  [{t}] Logging: {m}"))
broker.subscribe("data.updated", lambda t, m: print(f"  [{t}] Refreshing: {m}"))

Program 272: Template Engine (Mini Jinja)

import re

class TemplateEngine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.filters = {
            "upper": str.upper,
            "lower": str.lower,
            "title": str.title,
            "len": len,
        }
    
    def render(self, template, context):
        # Variable substitution: {{ var }}
        def replace_var(match):
            expr = match.group(1).strip()
            if '|' in expr:
                var, filter_name = expr.split('|', 1)
                value = context.get(var.strip(), '')
                return str(self.filters.get(filter_name.strip(), str)(value))
            return str(context.get(expr, ''))
        
        result = re.sub(r'{{(.+?)}}', replace_var, template)
        
        # For loops: {% for item in list %}...{% endfor %}
        def replace_loop(match):
            var, list_name, body = match.group(1), match.group(2), match.group(3)
            items = context.get(list_name, [])
            return ''.join(self.render(body, {**context, var: item}) for item in items)
        
        result = re.sub(r'{%\s*for\s+(\w+)\s+in\s+(\w+)\s*%}(.+?){%\s*endfor\s*%}',
                       replace_loop, result, flags=re.DOTALL)
        return result

engine = TemplateEngine()
template = """Hello {{ name | upper }}!
Items: {% for item in items %}[{{ item }}] {% endfor %}"""
print(engine.render(template, {"name": "alice", "items": ["a", "b", "c"]}))

# 832: Memory profiler
import sys
def deep_sizeof(obj, seen=None):
    seen = seen or set()
    obj_id = id(obj)
    if obj_id in seen:
        return 0
    seen.add(obj_id)
    size = sys.getsizeof(obj)
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        size += sum(deep_sizeof(k, seen) + deep_sizeof(v, seen) for k, v in obj.items())
    elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple, set)):
        size += sum(deep_sizeof(i, seen) for i in obj)
    return size

    pct = current / total
    filled = int(width * pct)
    bar = '█' * filled + '░' * (width - filled)
    print(f'\r|{bar}| {pct:.1%} [{current}/{total}]', end='', flush=True)

class Container:
    def __init__(self):
        self._factories = {}
        self._singletons = {}
    def register(self, name, factory, singleton=False):
        self._factories[name] = (factory, singleton)
    def resolve(self, name):
        factory, singleton = self._factories[name]
        if singleton:
            if name not in self._singletons:
                self._singletons[name] = factory()
            return self._singletons[name]
        return factory()

# 846: State machine
class StateMachine:
    def __init__(self, initial):
        self.state = initial
        self.transitions = {}
    def add_transition(self, from_state, event, to_state, action=None):
        self.transitions[(from_state, event)] = (to_state, action)
    def trigger(self, event):
        key = (self.state, event)
        if key in self.transitions:
            new_state, action = self.transitions[key]
            if action: action()
            self.state = new_state
            return True
        return False

def reservoir_sample(stream, k):
    reservoir = []
    for i, item in enumerate(stream):
        if i < k:
            reservoir.append(item)
        else:
            j = random.randint(0, i)
            if j < k:
                reservoir[j] = item

# 848: LRU Cache implementation
from collections import OrderedDict
class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        self.cache = OrderedDict()
        self.capacity = capacity
    def get(self, key):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache.move_to_end(key)
            return self.cache[key]
        return -1
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache.move_to_end(key)
        self.cache[key] = value
        if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
            self.cache.popitem(last=False)

# 849: Bloom filter
import hashlib
class BloomFilter:
    def __init__(self, size=1000, num_hashes=3):
        self.size = size
        self.bits = [False] * size
        self.num_hashes = num_hashes
    def _hashes(self, item):
        for i in range(self.num_hashes):
            h = int(hashlib.sha256(f"{item}{i}".encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % self.size
            yield h
    def add(self, item):
        for h in self._hashes(item):
            self.bits[h] = True
    def contains(self, item):
        return all(self.bits[h] for h in self._hashes(item))

import signal
class GracefulShutdown:
    def __init__(self):
        self.shutdown_requested = False
        self.handlers = []
    def register(self, handler):
        self.handlers.append(handler)
    def _handle_signal(self, signum, frame):
        self.shutdown_requested = True
        for h in self.handlers:
            h()
    def activate(self):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, self._handle_signal)

def flatten_dict(d, parent_key='', sep='.'):
    items = []
    for k, v in d.items():
        new_key = f"{parent_key}{sep}{k}" if parent_key else k
        if isinstance(v, dict):
            items.extend(flatten_dict(v, new_key, sep).items())
        else:
            items.append((new_key, v))
    return dict(items)

def unflatten_dict(d, sep='.'):
    result = {}
    for key, value in d.items():
        parts = key.split(sep)
        target = result
        for part in parts[:-1]:
            target = target.setdefault(part, {})
        target[parts[-1]] = value
    return result

def rolling_average(values, window=3):
    result = []
    for i in range(len(values)):
        start = max(0, i - window + 1)
        result.append(sum(values[start:i+1]) / (i - start + 1))
    return result

    for v in values[1:]:
        result.append(alpha * v + (1 - alpha) * result[-1])
    return result

def dict_diff(old, new):
    added = {k: new[k] for k in set(new) - set(old)}
    removed = {k: old[k] for k in set(old) - set(new)}
    changed = {k: (old[k], new[k]) for k in set(old) & set(new) if old[k] != new[k]}
    return {"added": added, "removed": removed, "changed": changed}

# 861: Retry decorator with count
from functools import wraps
def retry(max_attempts=3, exceptions=(Exception,)):
    def decorator(func):
        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            for attempt in range(max_attempts):
                try:
                    return func(*args, **kwargs)
                except exceptions as e:
                    if attempt == max_attempts - 1:
                        raise
                    print(f"  Retry {attempt+1}/{max_attempts}: {e}")
        return wrapper
    return decorator
attempt_count = 0
@retry(max_attempts=3)
def unstable():
    global attempt_count
    attempt_count += 1
    if attempt_count < 3:
        raise ValueError("Not ready")

# 863: Semaphore for resource limiting
import threading
def limited_parallel(tasks, max_concurrent=3):
    sem = threading.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
    results = [None] * len(tasks)
    def run(i, task):
        with sem:
            results[i] = task()
    threads = [threading.Thread(target=run, args=(i, t)) for i, t in enumerate(tasks)]
    for t in threads: t.start()
    for t in threads: t.join()
    return results

# 864: Chain of responsibility
class Handler:
    def __init__(self, name, can_handle):
        self.name = name
        self.can_handle = can_handle
        self.next = None
    def handle(self, request):
        if self.can_handle(request):
            return f"{self.name} handled: {request}"
        if self.next:
            return self.next.handle(request)
        return f"Unhandled: {request}"

# 865: Debounce function
import time
def debounce(wait):
    def decorator(func):
        last_call = [0]
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            now = time.time()
            if now - last_call[0] >= wait:
                last_call[0] = now
                return func(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapper
    return decorator
@debounce(0.1)
def save(data):
    print(f"  Saved: {data}")
save("v1"); save("v2"); time.sleep(0.15); save("v3")

# 866: Object pool
class ObjectPool:
    def __init__(self, factory, max_size=10):
        self.factory = factory
        self.pool = [factory() for _ in range(max_size)]
    def acquire(self):
        return self.pool.pop() if self.pool else self.factory()
    def release(self, obj):
        self.pool.append(obj)
pool = ObjectPool(lambda: {"buffer": bytearray(1024)}, max_size=3)
obj = pool.acquire()
print(f"Acquired. Pool size: {len(pool.pool)}")
pool.release(obj)
print(f"Released. Pool size: {len(pool.pool)}")

# 867: DAG executor
from collections import defaultdict
def topological_sort(graph):
    in_degree = defaultdict(int)
    for node in graph:
        for dep in graph[node]:
            in_degree[dep] += 1
    queue = [n for n in graph if in_degree[n] == 0]
    order = []
    while queue:
        node = queue.pop(0)
        order.append(node)
        for dep in graph.get(node, []):
            in_degree[dep] -= 1
            if in_degree[dep] == 0:
                queue.append(dep)
    return order
dag = {"data_load": ["preprocess"], "preprocess": ["train"], "train": ["evaluate"], "evaluate": []}
print(f"Execution order: {topological_sort(dag)}")

class IdempotencyTracker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.seen = {}
    def execute_once(self, key, func, *args):
        if key in self.seen:
            return self.seen[key]
        result = func(*args)
        self.seen[key] = result
        return result

import time

    def __init__(self, min_interval=1.0):
        self.min_interval = min_interval
        self.last_time = 0
    def wait(self):
        elapsed = time.time() - self.last_time

            time.sleep(self.min_interval - elapsed)
        self.last_time = time.time()

# 875: A/B testing framework
import random, hashlib
class ABTest:
    def __init__(self, name, variants, weights=None):
        self.name = name
        self.variants = variants
        self.weights = weights or [1/len(variants)] * len(variants)
        self.results = {v: {"count": 0, "conversions": 0} for v in variants}
    def assign(self, user_id):
        h = int(hashlib.md5(f"{self.name}:{user_id}".encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % 100
        cumulative = 0
        for v, w in zip(self.variants, self.weights):
            cumulative += w * 100
            if h < cumulative:
                self.results[v]["count"] += 1
                return v
    def record_conversion(self, variant):
        self.results[variant]["conversions"] += 1
    def report(self):
        for v, r in self.results.items():
            rate = r["conversions"] / r["count"] if r["count"] else 0
            print(f"  {v}: {r['count']} users, {r['conversions']} conv, {rate:.1%} rate")
ab = ABTest("model_version", ["v1", "v2"])
for uid in range(100):
    variant = ab.assign(f"user_{uid}")
    if random.random() < (0.1 if variant == "v1" else 0.15):
        ab.record_conversion(variant)
ab.report()

        self.new = new_handler
        self.canary_pct = canary_pct

import secrets, time
class APIKeyManager:
    def __init__(self):
        self.keys = {}
    def generate(self, user, ttl=3600):
        key = secrets.token_hex(16)
        self.keys[key] = {"user": user, "created": time.time(), "ttl": ttl}
        return key
    def validate(self, key):
        if key not in self.keys:
            return None
        info = self.keys[key]
        if time.time() - info["created"] > info["ttl"]:
            del self.keys[key]
            return None
        return info["user"]

# 879: Request batch processor
class BatchProcessor:
    def __init__(self, process_fn, batch_size=10, max_wait=1.0):
        self.process_fn = process_fn
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.buffer = []
    def add(self, item):
        self.buffer.append(item)
        if len(self.buffer) >= self.batch_size:
            return self.flush()
    def flush(self):
        if not self.buffer:
            return []
        results = self.process_fn(self.buffer)
        self.buffer = []
        return results

class ServiceDefinition:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        self.methods = {}
    def method(self, name, input_type=None, output_type=None):
        def decorator(func):
            self.methods[name] = {"handler": func, "input": input_type, "output": output_type}
            return func
        return decorator
    def call(self, method_name, data):
        if method_name not in self.methods:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown method: {method_name}")
        return self.methods[method_name]["handler"](data)

# 883: Timeout decorator
import threading
def timeout(seconds):
    def decorator(func):
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            result = [None]
            error = [None]
            def target():
                try:
                    result[0] = func(*args, **kwargs)
                except Exception as e:
                    error[0] = e
            t = threading.Thread(target=target)
            t.start()
            t.join(seconds)
            if t.is_alive():
                raise TimeoutError(f"Function timed out after {seconds}s")
            if error[0]:
                raise error[0]
            return result[0]
        return wrapper
    return decorator

# 885: Consistent hashing
import hashlib
class ConsistentHash:
    def __init__(self, nodes, replicas=3):
        self.ring = {}
        for node in nodes:
            for i in range(replicas):
                key = int(hashlib.md5(f"{node}:{i}".encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
                self.ring[key] = node
        self.sorted_keys = sorted(self.ring)
    def get_node(self, key):
        h = int(hashlib.md5(str(key).encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        for ring_key in self.sorted_keys:
            if h <= ring_key:
                return self.ring[ring_key]
        return self.ring[self.sorted_keys[0]]

class GracefulService:

        self.fallbacks = {}
    def register(self, name, primary, fallback):
        self.fallbacks[name] = (primary, fallback)
    def call(self, name, *args):

        try:

        except Exception:
            return fallback(*args)

# 889: Request deduplication
class RequestDedup:
    def __init__(self, window=60):
        self.seen = {}
        self.window = window
    def is_duplicate(self, request_hash):
        now = time.time()
        self.seen = {k: v for k, v in self.seen.items() if now - v < self.window}
        if request_hash in self.seen:
            return True
        self.seen[request_hash] = now
        return False

# 890: Shadow deployment
class ShadowDeploy:
    def __init__(self, primary, shadow):
        self.primary = primary
        self.shadow = shadow
        self.diffs = []
    def handle(self, request):
        primary_result = self.primary(request)
        try:
            shadow_result = self.shadow(request)
            if primary_result != shadow_result:
                self.diffs.append({"request": request, "primary": primary_result, "shadow": shadow_result})
        except Exception:
            pass
        return primary_result

class MetricsExporter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.counters = {}
        self.gauges = {}
    def inc_counter(self, name, value=1):
        self.counters[name] = self.counters.get(name, 0) + value
    def set_gauge(self, name, value):
        self.gauges[name] = value

        lines = []
        for name, value in self.counters.items():
            lines.append(f"{name} {value}")
        for name, value in self.gauges.items():
            lines.append(f"{name} {value}")

# 899: Blue-green deployment
class BlueGreenDeploy:
    def __init__(self):
        self.blue = None
        self.green = None
        self.active = "blue"
    def deploy(self, version, handler):
        target = "green" if self.active == "blue" else "blue"
        setattr(self, target, {"version": version, "handler": handler})
        return target
    def switch(self):
        self.active = "green" if self.active == "blue" else "blue"
    def handle(self, request):
        handler = getattr(self, self.active)
        return handler["handler"](request) if handler else None

# 900: Complete microservice template
class Microservice:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        self.routes = {}
        self.middleware = []
        self.health = True
    def route(self, path):
        def decorator(func):
            self.routes[path] = func
            return func
        return decorator
    def use(self, middleware):
        self.middleware.append(middleware)
    def handle(self, path, request):
        for mw in self.middleware:
            request = mw(request)
        handler = self.routes.get(path)
        if handler:
            return {"status": 200, "body": handler(request)}
        return {"status": 404, "body": "Not found"}

import http.server
import json
import threading
import urllib.request

class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        body = json.dumps({"path": self.path, "ok": True}).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass                      # keep the test output clean

server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)

import http.server
import json
import threading
import urllib.request

class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers["Content-Length"])
        payload = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length))
        body = json.dumps({"received": payload, "n": len(payload)}).encode()
        self.send_response(201)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
port = server.server_address[1]
threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

Program 281: TCP Is a Stream, Not a Message Queue

import socket
import threading

received = []

def serve(sock):
    conn, _ = sock.accept()
    with conn:
        chunk = conn.recv(4096)            # ONE recv, three sends
        received.append(chunk)

server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
server.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
server.listen(1)
port = server.getsockname()[1]
t = threading.Thread(target=serve, args=(server,))
t.start()

with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port)) as c:
    c.sendall(b"one")
    c.sendall(b"two")
    c.sendall(b"three")
t.join()
server.close()

print(b"".join(received))          # Output: b'onetwothree'
print("message boundaries are gone:", received[0] != b"one")
# Output: message boundaries are gone: True

# This is why every TCP protocol needs framing: a length prefix, or a delimiter.

Program 282: Length-Prefixed Framing Over TCP

import socket
import struct
import threading

def send_msg(sock, payload):
    sock.sendall(struct.pack("!I", len(payload)) + payload)   # 4-byte length first

def recv_exactly(sock, n):
    buf = b""
    while len(buf) < n:
        chunk = sock.recv(n - len(buf))
        if not chunk:
            raise ConnectionError("socket closed early")
        buf += chunk
    return buf

def recv_msg(sock):
    (length,) = struct.unpack("!I", recv_exactly(sock, 4))
    return recv_exactly(sock, length)

got = []

def serve(sock):
    conn, _ = sock.accept()
    with conn:
        for _ in range(3):
            got.append(recv_msg(conn))

server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
server.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
server.listen(1)
port = server.getsockname()[1]
t = threading.Thread(target=serve, args=(server,))
t.start()

with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port)) as c:
    for msg in (b"one", b"two", b"three"):
        send_msg(c, msg)
t.join()
server.close()

print(got)          # Output: [b'one', b'two', b'three']

Program 285: Retrying a Request with Backoff and a Cap

import http.server
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

attempts = {"n": 0}

class Flaky(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        attempts["n"] += 1
        code = 200 if attempts["n"] >= 3 else 503     # fails twice, then works
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", "2")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"ok")

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Flaky)
port = server.server_address[1]
threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

def get_with_retry(url, tries=5, base=0.01, cap=0.5):
    for i in range(tries):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as r:
                return r.status
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            if e.code < 500 or i == tries - 1:
                raise                       # 4xx will never succeed on retry
            time.sleep(min(base * 2 ** i, cap))

print(get_with_retry(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/"))    # Output: 200
print("attempts made:", attempts["n"])                # Output: attempts made: 3
server.shutdown()

Program 286: Setting a Timeout So a Request Cannot Hang

import socket
import threading
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

listener = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
listener.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
listener.listen(1)
port = listener.getsockname()[1]

def accept_and_stall():
    conn, _ = listener.accept()
    import time; time.sleep(3)      # accept the connection, then never reply
    conn.close()

threading.Thread(target=accept_and_stall, daemon=True).start()

try:
    urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/", timeout=0.3)
except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, socket.timeout) as e:
    print("timed out rather than hanging")
    # Output: timed out rather than hanging
listener.close()

# A request with no timeout waits for ever by default. In a request handler that
# is one hung upstream away from exhausting your whole thread pool.

Program 289: Concurrent Requests Beat Sequential Ones

import http.server

import threading
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

class Slow(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        time.sleep(0.2)

        self.send_header("Content-Length", "2")
        self.end_headers()

for _ in range(5):
    urllib.request.urlopen(url).read()
serial = time.perf_counter() - start

start = time.perf_counter()
with ThreadPoolExecutor(5) as pool:
    list(pool.map(lambda _: urllib.request.urlopen(url).read(), range(5)))
concurrent = time.perf_counter() - start

print("serial took longer:", serial > concurrent * 1.5)

Program 290: A Tiny Router for a Request Path

import re

ROUTES = []

def route(pattern):
    regex = re.compile("^" + re.sub(r"<(\w+)>", r"(?P<\1>[^/]+)", pattern) + "$")
    def register(fn):
        ROUTES.append((regex, fn))
        return fn
    return register

@route("/users/<user_id>")
def get_user(user_id):
    return f"user {user_id}"

@route("/users/<user_id>/posts/<post_id>")
def get_post(user_id, post_id):
    return f"post {post_id} by user {user_id}"

def dispatch(path):
    for regex, fn in ROUTES:
        m = regex.match(path)
        if m:
            return fn(**m.groupdict())
    return "404"

print(dispatch("/users/7"))                  # Output: user 7
print(dispatch("/users/7/posts/3"))          # Output: post 3 by user 7
print(dispatch("/nope"))                     # Output: 404

    return "Basic " + base64.b64encode(raw).decode()

def parse_header(header):
    scheme, _, payload = header.partition(" ")
    return base64.b64decode(payload).decode().split(":", 1)

Program 292: Signing a Payload with HMAC

import hashlib
import hmac

SECRET = b"shared-signing-key"

def sign(payload):
    return hmac.new(SECRET, payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

def verify(payload, signature):
    return hmac.compare_digest(sign(payload), signature)   # constant time

body = b'{"amount": 100}'
sig = sign(body)
print(len(sig))                                  # Output: 64
print(verify(body, sig))                         # Output: True
print(verify(b'{"amount": 999}', sig))           # Output: False

# compare_digest, not ==: a normal comparison returns early on the first
# differing byte, which leaks the correct prefix through timing.

Program 293: A Token-Bucket Rate Limiter

import time

class TokenBucket:
    def __init__(self, capacity, refill_per_second):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.tokens = capacity
        self.rate = refill_per_second
        self.last = time.monotonic()

    def allow(self, cost=1):
        now = time.monotonic()
        self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + (now - self.last) * self.rate)
        self.last = now
        if self.tokens >= cost:
            self.tokens -= cost
            return True
        return False

bucket = TokenBucket(capacity=3, refill_per_second=100)
print([bucket.allow() for _ in range(5)])
# Output: [True, True, True, False, False]
time.sleep(0.05)                     # 0.05s * 100/s = 5 tokens, capped at 3
print(bucket.allow())                # Output: True

# A bucket allows a burst up to capacity, then settles to the refill rate -
# which is what real APIs mean by "100 requests per second, burst 300".

Program 295: Content Negotiation from the Accept Header

def best_match(accept_header, supported):
    """Parse 'type;q=0.8, other' and pick the highest-quality supported type."""
    options = []
    for part in accept_header.split(","):
        bits = part.strip().split(";")
        media = bits[0].strip()
        q = 1.0
        for b in bits[1:]:
            if b.strip().startswith("q="):
                q = float(b.strip()[2:])
        options.append((q, media))
    for _, media in sorted(options, key=lambda x: -x[0]):
        if media in supported:
            return media
        if media == "*/*":
            return supported[0]
    return None

SUPPORTED = ["application/json", "text/html"]
print(best_match("text/html", SUPPORTED))                        # Output: text/html
print(best_match("application/xml;q=0.9, application/json;q=0.8", SUPPORTED))
# Output: application/json
print(best_match("*/*", SUPPORTED))                              # Output: application/json
print(best_match("image/png", SUPPORTED))                        # Output: None

Program 296: Idempotency Keys Stop Duplicate Charges

processed = {}

def charge(idempotency_key, amount):
    if idempotency_key in processed:
        return processed[idempotency_key], "replayed"
    charge_id = f"ch_{len(processed) + 1}"
    processed[idempotency_key] = charge_id
    return charge_id, "created"

print(charge("key-abc", 100))       # Output: ('ch_1', 'created')
print(charge("key-abc", 100))       # Output: ('ch_1', 'replayed')
print(charge("key-xyz", 250))       # Output: ('ch_2', 'created')
print(len(processed))               # Output: 2

# The client retries after a timeout with the SAME key, so a lost response
# cannot become a second charge.

Q101. Parsing a URL into its parts — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
from urllib.parse import urlparse
u = urlparse("https://user:pw@api.example.com:8443/v1/items?q=a+b&n=2#top")
print(u.scheme, u.hostname, u.port)

print(u.query)
print(u.fragment)

Answer: 

https api.example.com 8443
/v1/items 
q=a+b&n=2
top

Explanation: hostname is lowercased and strips the credentials and port, while netloc keeps all of them. The fragment never leaves the browser - a server never sees #top.

print(parse_qsl(q))

Answer: 

{'tag': ['a', 'b'], 'page': ['2']}
[('tag', 'a'), ('tag', 'b'), ('page', '2')]
['2']

Explanation: parse_qs maps every key to a LIST because a query string may repeat a key. Indexing ["page"] gives ['2'], not '2' - forgetting the [0] is a very common bug.

print(quote("/x/y"), quote("/x/y", safe=""))

q=a%26b+c&path=%2Fx%2Fy
a%26b%20c
a%26b+c
/x/y %2Fx%2Fy

Explanation: quote leaves / alone by default because it is a path separator; quote_plus encodes a space as + for query strings while quote uses %20. Building a URL by string concatenation skips all of this.

[b'AAABBBCCC']

threading.Thread(target=serve, daemon=True).start()
with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port)) as c:
    chunk = c.recv(1024)
    print(len(chunk), chunk)
    print(c.recv(1024))
srv.close()

5 b'12345'

Explanation: recv(1024) is an upper bound. An empty bytes object means the peer closed - that is the ONLY reliable end-of-stream signal, and treating it as 'no data yet' is an infinite loop.

Q111. struct packing is fixed width and endian-sensitive — what is the output?

import struct
print(struct.pack("!I", 1))
print(struct.pack("<I", 1))
print(struct.calcsize("!I"), struct.calcsize("!H"))
print(struct.unpack("!I", b"\x00\x00\x01\x00"))

Answer: 

b'\x00\x00\x00\x01'
b'\x01\x00\x00\x00'
4 2
(256,)

Explanation: ! is network byte order (big-endian) and is what every wire protocol specifies. Packing with the native < on one machine and unpacking with ! on another silently produces the wrong number.

4 5
{'Content-Length': '5'}

Explanation: The header counts BYTES. Using the string length under-counts by one per multi-byte character, and the client hangs waiting for a body that already ended.

•

Q113. Status codes: which are safe to retry — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
codes = {200: "ok", 301: "moved", 400: "bad request", 401: "unauthorised",
         429: "rate limited", 500: "server error", 503: "unavailable"}
retryable = [c for c in codes if c == 429 or 500 <= c < 600]
print(sorted(codes))
print(sorted(retryable))

Answer: 

[200, 301, 400, 401, 429, 500, 503]
[429, 500, 503]

Explanation: Retrying a 4xx repeats the same failure - the request itself is wrong. Only 429 and 5xx are worth retrying, and 429 should honour Retry-After rather than a fixed backoff.

•

Q114. Idempotency of HTTP methods — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
methods = {"GET": True, "HEAD": True, "PUT": True, "DELETE": True,
           "POST": False, "PATCH": False}
print([m for m, safe in sorted(methods.items()) if safe])
print([m for m, safe in sorted(methods.items()) if not safe])

Answer: 

['DELETE', 'GET', 'HEAD', 'PUT']
['PATCH', 'POST']

Explanation: An idempotent method can be retried after a timeout without changing the outcome. POST cannot, which is why payment APIs require an idempotency key.

•

Q115. Timeouts are not set by default — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import socket
s = socket.socket()
print(s.gettimeout())
s.settimeout(0.5)
print(s.gettimeout())
print(socket.getdefaulttimeout())
s.close()

Answer: 

None
0.5
None

Explanation: None means block for ever. A single unresponsive upstream with no timeout will pin a worker thread until the OS gives up, which can be minutes.

•

Q116. Exponential backoff with a cap — what is the output?

base, cap = 0.1, 2.0
delays = [min(base * 2 ** i, cap) for i in range(8)]
print(delays)
print(sum(delays))

Answer: 

[0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.6, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0]
9.1

Explanation: Uncapped doubling reaches minutes by the tenth attempt. Real clients also add jitter, otherwise every client that failed together retries together and re-creates the spike.

•

Q117. JSON round-trips lose Python types — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import json
original = {"n": 1, "t": (1, 2), "s": {1, 2}, "k": 5}
try:
    json.dumps(original)
except TypeError as e:
    print("TypeError")
print(json.dumps({"n": 1, "t": (1, 2)}))
print(json.loads(json.dumps({"t": (1, 2)})))
print(json.loads('{"1": "a"}'))

Answer: 

TypeError
{"n": 1, "t": [1, 2]}
{'t': [1, 2]}
{'1': 'a'}

Explanation: A tuple becomes a list and never comes back; a set cannot be encoded at all; and every JSON key is a string, so integer keys come back as strings.

•

Q118. JSON booleans and nulls have different names — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import json
print(json.dumps({"a": True, "b": None, "c": float("1e400")}))
print(json.loads('{"a": true, "b": null}'))
print(json.dumps({"a": 1.0}))

Answer: 

{"a": true, "b": null, "c": Infinity}
{'a': True, 'b': None}
{"a": 1.0}

Explanation: JSON writes true/null in lowercase, and Python's encoder emits Infinity, which is NOT valid JSON - a strict parser on the other end will reject it. Pass allow_nan=False to find out early.

Q119. Base64 is encoding, not encryption — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import base64
secret = b"password123"
enc = base64.b64encode(secret)
print(enc)
print(base64.b64decode(enc))
print(len(secret), len(enc))

Answer: 

b'cGFzc3dvcmQxMjM='
b'password123'
11 16

Explanation: Anyone can reverse it with one call. Base64 exists to move bytes through text-only channels; Basic auth over plain HTTP is a password sent in the clear.

Q120. Comparing secrets in constant time — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import hmac
a = "abc123token"
print(a == "abc123token")
print(hmac.compare_digest(a, "abc123token"))
print(hmac.compare_digest(a, "abc123toke_"))

Answer: 

True
True
False

Explanation: == returns as soon as two bytes differ, so response time leaks how much of the prefix was right. compare_digest always examines the whole value.

Q121. A dict is not a stable API response — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import json
a = {"b": 1, "a": 2}
print(json.dumps(a))
print(json.dumps(a, sort_keys=True))
print(list(a))

Answer: 

{"b": 1, "a": 2}
{"a": 2, "b": 1}
['b', 'a']

Explanation: Python preserves insertion order, so the JSON matches the order you built it in - not alphabetical. Any client or test that compares response strings needs sort_keys=True on both sides.

Q122. Reading a response body twice — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import http.server, threading, urllib.request

class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", "5")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"hello")
    def log_message(self, *a): pass

s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
threading.Thread(target=s.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{s.server_address[1]}/") as r:
    print(r.read())
    print(r.read())
s.shutdown()

Answer: 

b'hello'
b''

Explanation: The body is a stream: once consumed it is gone. Anything that needs the payload twice must keep the first read in a variable.

Q123. Headers you send versus headers you get — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import http.server, threading, urllib.request

class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("X-Custom", "server-value")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
        self.end_headers()
    def log_message(self, *a): pass

s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
threading.Thread(target=s.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{s.server_address[1]}/",
                             headers={"X-Sent": "client-value"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
    print(r.headers["X-Custom"])
    print(r.headers.get("X-Sent"))
    print(r.headers.get("Server") is not None)
s.shutdown()

Answer: 

server-value
None
True

Explanation: Response headers contain only what the SERVER sent. Your request headers are not echoed back unless the server chooses to.

Q124. IP address parsing and validation — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import ipaddress
a = ipaddress.ip_address("192.168.1.10")
print(a.version, a.is_private)
print(ipaddress.ip_address("8.8.8.8").is_private)
net = ipaddress.ip_network("10.0.0.0/30")
print(list(net.hosts()))
print(a in ipaddress.ip_network("192.168.1.0/24"))

Answer: 

4 True
False
[IPv4Address('10.0.0.1'), IPv4Address('10.0.0.2')]
True

Explanation: ipaddress validates and does subnet maths for you. hosts() excludes the network and broadcast addresses, which is why a /30 yields only two usable hosts.

Q125. Hostname resolution can return several addresses — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import socket
info = socket.getaddrinfo("localhost", 80, proto=socket.IPPROTO_TCP)
families = sorted({socket.AddressFamily(i[0]).name for i in info})
print(len(info) >= 1)
print(all(len(i) == 5 for i in info))
print("AF_INET" in families or "AF_INET6" in families)

Answer: 

True
True
True

Explanation: One name can map to several addresses and families. Hard-coding AF_INET is how a service breaks the day the host gets an IPv6 record.

Q126. A socket in TIME_WAIT blocks rebinding — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import socket
a = socket.socket()
a.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
a.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
port = a.getsockname()[1]
print(port > 0)
a.close()
b = socket.socket()
b.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
b.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
print("rebound after close")
b.close()

Answer: 

True
rebound after close

Explanation: Without SO_REUSEADDR a restarted server often fails with 'address already in use' because the old socket lingers in TIME_WAIT for up to two minutes.

Q127. Cookies are strings with attributes — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
from http.cookies import SimpleCookie
c = SimpleCookie()
c["sid"] = "abc"
c["sid"]["path"] = "/"
c["sid"]["httponly"] = True
out = c.output(header="Set-Cookie:")
print("sid=abc" in out)
print("HttpOnly" in out)
incoming = SimpleCookie(); incoming.load("sid=abc; theme=dark")
print(sorted(incoming.keys()))

Answer: 

True
True
['sid', 'theme']

Explanation: The Cookie header the browser sends back carries name=value ONLY - Path, HttpOnly and Secure are instructions to the browser and never come back.

Q128. Percent-encoding is not idempotent — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
from urllib.parse import quote, unquote
s = "a b"
once = quote(s)
twice = quote(once)
print(once)
print(twice)
print(unquote(twice))
print(unquote(unquote(twice)))

Answer: 

a%20b
a%2520b
a%20b
a b

Explanation: Encoding an already-encoded string escapes the % itself, so one decode gives you the encoded form back rather than the original. Double-encoding is a very common cause of '%2520' appearing in logs.

Q129. Chunked responses have no Content-Length — what is the output?

AnswerExplanation 
import http.server, threading, urllib.request

class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
        self.end_headers()
        for part in (b"aaa", b"bb"):
            self.wfile.write(b"%x\r\n%s\r\n" % (len(part), part))
        self.wfile.write(b"0\r\n\r\n")
    def log_message(self, *a): pass

s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
threading.Thread(target=s.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{s.server_address[1]}/") as r:
    print(r.headers.get("Content-Length"))
    print(r.read())
s.shutdown()

Answer: 

None
b'aaabb'

Explanation: With chunked encoding the length is unknown up front, so you cannot pre-allocate or show a progress bar - you read until the zero-length chunk.

Q130. Rate limiting arithmetic — what is the output?

AnswerExplanationFrom the runnable 650-program setOutput 
capacity, refill_per_sec = 10, 2
tokens = capacity
requests = 15
allowed = 0
for _ in range(requests):
    if tokens >= 1:
        tokens -= 1
        allowed += 1
print(allowed, requests - allowed)
print(capacity + refill_per_sec * 5)

Answer: 

10 5
20

Explanation: A burst of 15 against a bucket of 10 lets 10 through immediately and rejects 5. After five seconds of refill the bucket would allow 10 again - capacity is the burst, the refill rate is the sustained limit.

Program 309: JWT

print("Q475: JWT")
print("  JSON Web Token: self-contained, signed token.")
print("  Structure: header.payload.signature (base64url encoded)")
print("  Contains: sub, exp, iat, iss + custom claims")
print("  Verify signature, check expiration, extract claims")
import json, base64, hmac, hashlib

def create_simple_jwt(payload, secret):
    header = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({"alg": "HS256"}).encode()).decode().rstrip('=')
    body = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps(payload).encode()).decode().rstrip('=')
    sig = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{header}.{body}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:16]
    return f"{header}.{body}.{sig}"

token = create_simple_jwt({"sub": "user123", "role": "admin"}, "secret")
print(f"  Simple JWT: {token[:50]}...")
print()

Program 312: Rate limiting

print("Q478: Rate limiting")
print("  Limit requests per client per time window.")
print("  Algorithms: fixed window, sliding window, token bucket, leaky bucket")
print("  Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After")
print("  Implementation: Redis counters with TTL")

class TokenBucket:
    """Token bucket rate limiter."""
    def __init__(self, rate, capacity):
        self.rate = rate
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.tokens = capacity
        import time
        self.last_refill = time.monotonic()

    def allow(self):
        import time
        now = time.monotonic()
        elapsed = now - self.last_refill
        self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + elapsed * self.rate)
        self.last_refill = now
        if self.tokens >= 1:
            self.tokens -= 1
            return True
        return False

limiter = TokenBucket(rate=10, capacity=10)
results = [limiter.allow() for _ in range(12)]
print(f"  12 requests, 10 capacity: {sum(results)} allowed")
print()

Output 

Q478: Rate limiting
  Limit requests per client per time window.
  Algorithms: fixed window, sliding window, token bucket, leaky bucket
  Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After
  Implementation: Redis counters with TTL
  12 requests, 10 capacity: 10 allowed
